That sounds worrying. Do you mean “dead” as in outages, leadership/news, pricing/policy changes, or that you’re thinking of moving off OpenAI?

I don’t have live news, but here’s how you can protect yourself and plan next steps, whatever the situation:
- Check current status: status.openai.com and the official blog/help center for announcements.
- Safeguard your work: export chats you need, back up prompts, system messages, fine-tune configs, eval datasets, and any embeddings/vector stores you control.
- De-risk your stack: add a model/provider abstraction layer so you can switch models with minimal code change.
- Map features: list which OpenAI features you rely on (chat, function calling/tools, JSON mode, fine-tuning, vision, audio, batch, Assistants, etc.) and note required equivalents.
- Run quick evals: create a small benchmark of your key tasks to compare candidate models.

If you are considering alternatives, common options include:
- Closed-source APIs: Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), Cohere.
- Open-weight models via providers or self-hosting: Llama 3.x/3.1, Llama Guard, Mistral/Mixtral, Qwen, Phi-4, etc. (via together.ai, Fireworks, Replicate, AWS Bedrock, Azure, GCP, or your own GPUs).

I can help you:
- Audit your current usage and identify blockers.
- Propose drop-in replacements and a migration plan.
- Build an eval harness and prompt/temperature parity tests.
- Draft a data export checklist tailored to your setup.

Tell me what specifically has you concerned and what you’re using OpenAI for, and I’ll give you a concrete, minimal-change plan.
